propositions: Self-hosted Jira Data Center uses REST v2 with wiki-markup bodies, PAT bearer auth, and name-based user identity, while Cloud uses REST v3 with ADF, ACLI subprocess auth, and accountId; PR #120 proposed a forked adapter that privately imported shared code and duplicated field-mapping logic without a pinned contract.

Six symbols from the jira adapter are needed by both Cloud and DC backends (field maps, sanitizers, probe classifier, link relations), but they exist as independent copies or are reached through private imports, creating drift risk and preventing single-sourced maintenance.

Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) are loaded by path via _loader.py and cannot be relocated without breaking the dynamic loader, but their contents can be edited to import from a shared jira_family layer via dependency inversion.

The rich-text codec (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for DC) and user-identity model (accountId for Cloud, name for DC) are intrinsically different per deployment and must be parameterized as shared contracts with separate implementations, not unified into a single code path.

DC requires HTTPS with certificate verification always on (never verify=False), rejects plain-HTTP base_url unless allow_insecure=true is set, and reads the PAT credential from JIRA_PAT environment variable only (never from config file), plus supports operator-configured resolved-status names via reconciler.resolved_statuses.

The epic extracts and unifies shared logic via a new jira_family sub-seam with machine-checked import boundaries, delivers DC backend built on the pycontribs/jira library as an optional extra, and verifies bidirectional reconciliation against a real Jira 8.17.1 Data Center instance before closing.
